paper.title: RLVE: Scaling Up Reinforcement Learning for Language Models with Adaptive Verifiable Environments
paper.central_claim: Training LMs with RL on procedurally generated verifiable environments whose difficulty adapts to the policy (RLVE), using 400 hand-engineered environments (RLVE-Gym), scales RL: environment scaling improves generalization to unseen environments and joint training on all 400 yields +3.37% average over six reasoning benchmarks from ProRL-1.5B-v2 versus +0.49% for continued RLVR with over 3x compute.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured model type only

sections_read: Appendix A/B/C/D/E headings and evaluation-setup passages (skimmed, environment catalogue not read line by line)

evidence.quote: yields a 3.37% absolute average improvement across six reasoning benchmarks, starting from one of the strongest 1.5B reasoning LMs.
evidence.support_explanation: The reported retained improvement is in the policy model's benchmark performance, i.e. the product is trained weights.

evidence.quote: Any algorithm applicable to RLVR can be directly applied to RLVE
evidence.support_explanation: Learning update is a standard weight-updating RL algorithm (DAPO/GRPO variant); RLVE is an environment/data layer for it.

evidence.quote: is considered proficient at this difficulty level, and the upper bound is incremented by one
evidence.support_explanation: The only feedback-driven non-weight state is a per-environment difficulty upper bound incremented when rollout accuracy passes a threshold; it is reset-free scalar training state inside one run, not a retained prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator.

evidence.quote: In our preliminary explorations, we tried employing frontier LMs to perform automatic environment engineering.
evidence.support_explanation: Environment construction is not performed by the system from execution feedback; automatic environment engineering was tried and not adopted.

evidence.quote: In contrast, RLVE grounds environment adaptation in controllable manual construction, avoiding potentially incorrect LM-generated problems or verifiers.
evidence.support_explanation: Author explicitly separates RLVE from LM-generated (self-evolving) environments; the 400 environments are static human-written programs.

unresolved: Boundary question for aggregator: whether transient adaptive-difficulty controllers in weight-training curricula should ever count as harness-level components.

scope_analysis: Under SCORE_SPEC/EVIDENCE, weight-updating self-improvement and methods without a retained non-weight change are not included. The adaptive difficulty controller is a non-weight state derived from execution feedback, but it is transient within a single training run and is not claimed or measured as a retained artifact; RLVE-Gym is a static, hand-written resource. Domain card self_generate_the_curriculum is flagged as a boundary case touching weights; per rubric A3 the evaluated object here (policy weights) governs the scope decision. If the aggregator rules this boundary case in scope, it would be claim_type component_training with RS candidates around self_supervised_signal_engineering / generative_process_redesign; this seat has not scored it.
rationale: Weight-updating RL on static hand-built environments; transient difficulty scheduler; no retained non-weight component. Out of scope (rubric A3).
